title: incremental-snapshot-resume-protocol-and-tool-telemetry-scrapbook
body:
Context and intent:

This is a working sketch of a compact "incremental snapshot + resume" protocol for the Hosted API streaming surface. Goal is a lightweight, SDK-forward handshake that: preserves low-latency streaming, enables resumable sessions after client disconnects, provides first-class signals for tool invocation/commit telemetry, and makes structured partial-output practical for low-bandwidth/mobile clients.

Why this doc exists (notes to self):
- Many teams ask for resumable sessions but current proposals either (a) persist giant session blobs or (b) require full re-run of history. We want an option that is incremental, predictable cost, and interoperable with tool-calls and structured JSON fragments.
- Observability and telemetry for tool calls are currently ad-hoc; we want a compact event model so SRE + Product can reason about tool-latency, retries, and fallbacks.
- SDK ergonomics must make resume and partial commit easy rather than a footgun.

High level proposal summary:
- Streaming responses are emitted as a sequence of "frames". A subset of frames are "snapshot frames" which capture minimal resume state (KV references, last-ack token, tool-transcript markers).
- Client can request a resume by supplying the last acknowledged snapshot_id and a small client context. Server validates compatibility and resumes tokenized generation (no full re-synthesis) where possible.
- Tool calls are represented as separate frames with stable call_ids and idempotency tokens. Each tool-call frame emits telemetry events (call.sent, call.started, call.completed, call.failed) with short enumerated reasons.
- Structured-output: the model emits partial JSON fragments in "committed" frames. SDK provides a reassembly helper that tolerates omission and truncation and exposes a deterministic merge strategy.

Goals and success metrics:
- Resume successful for >85% of brief interruptions (client reconnect within 15s) without re-running model on server side.
- Reduce end-to-end token cost for resumed sessions by 40% vs naive re-run.
- Measure tool-call telemetry coverage: instrument at least 95% of tool calls across top 20 customers in alpha.
- SDK adoption: experimental beta integration in JS/TS SDK within 6 weeks; internal mobile SDK PoC within 10 weeks.

Non-goals:
- Full deterministic replay for arbitrary prompt mutation (we assume clients will not change earlier turns if they expect resume).
- Solving cross-region sticky-state replication in this initial design (we rely on multi-region fallbacks later).

User stories / example flows:
1) Mobile chat app, intermittent LTE: user types, gets streamed replies. App loses connectivity after receiving 65% of content. On reconnect, it sends resume(snapshot_id=abc, last_received_offset=0.65). Server sends missing frames and then continues continuing generation. App displays new tokens incrementally.

2) SaaS assistant that triggers a DB lookup tool: assistant emits a tool-call frame with call_id=tx-42 and idempotency=uuid-123. Agent runtime forwards to tool. Tool completes, returns result frame. If client disconnected mid-tool-call, resume logic ensures the tool status is replayed and not re-invoked if idempotency token seen.

Design details (protocol primitives):
- Frame types (short):
  - text_chunk: streaming text tokens (same as current incremental output)
  - snapshot_start / snapshot_delta / snapshot_commit: incremental snapshot machinery. Each snapshot has snapshot_id (short base62), parent_snapshot_id optional, and small payload of refs (list of opaque refs to server KV/cache).
  - tool_call: metadata about a tool invocation (call_id, idempotency_token, tool_name, args_hash)
  - tool_event: emitted lifecycle events referencing call_id (sent, queued, started, succeeded, failed-with-reason, canceled)
  - structured_fragment: partial structured-object fragment (map/array/primitive, encoded as newline-delimited JSON fragments with a fragment_seq)
  - checkpoint: small stable marker (human-visible) that client may choose to ack; server can garbage-collect snapshots older than N checkpoints.

Snapshot semantics (practical constraints):
- Snapshots are not full model caches. They are pointers to cached KV entries (prefix-key, KV-version) and small runtime state (narrow: last-layer-KV offsets, last-token-id, generation-seed).
- The server guarantees that presenting a snapshot_id that is still valid will allow continuing generation at semantic parity up to policy constraints (sequence length drift tolerated up to X tokens).
- Snapshots have TTLs; default TTL 5 minutes for free-tier, 1 hour for dedicated-committed. (configurable per customer)
- Snapshot size limit: 2KB compressed metadata. If a conversation's resume state exceeds that, server will emit a "snapshot_handoff" instruction telling client to switch to full re-run or a longer-lived dedicated snapshot (a.k.a. reserved checkpoint).

Resume handshake (suggested flow):
- Client reconnects and calls POST /v1/sessions/:session_id/resume with { snapshot_id, last_fragment_seq, client_sdk_version, want_rewind=false }
- Server validates snapshot_id. Responses:
  - 200 resumed -> stream starts with a "resume_preamble" frame describing resume plan and any missing fragments, followed by missing frames, then resumed generation frames.
  - 412 snapshot_mismatch -> server suggests fallback options (replay_required, resume_from_parent: <id>, offer_long_checkpoint: <url>)
  - 404 snapshot_expired -> must re-run; server may include quality-preserving hints (context_diffs).

Tool-call idempotency and telemetry model:
- All tool_call frames must include idempotency_token (client-provided or server-assigned). Server should persist seen idempotency_tokens per customer for TTL matching snapshot TTLs to avoid accidental double-exec.
- Telemetry events: minimal set {call.sent, call.dispatch, call.started, call.completed, call.failed}. Events carry small enums for reason codes (timeout, rate-limited, perm-denied, validation-error, network-error).
- Telemetry schema is intentionally thin: event_time, call_id, session_id, trace_id (optional), latency_ms (when relevant), outcome_code, tool_name. Keep payload size <512 bytes per event.
- Instrumentation: SDK emits local events (sdk.resume_attempt, sdk.snapshot_ack, sdk.tool_attempt) that map to server-side events for end-to-end traces. We will add a small sampling policy for high-volume customers.

Structured incremental output and assembly heuristics:
- Structured_fragment frames carry fragment_seq (monotonic), fragment_type (object/array/primitive), and partial_payload (a ndjson-friendly chunk).
- To avoid partial-JSON parse errors on the client, SDK will provide a reassembler with multiple strategies:
  - conservative-pass-through: buffer until full top-level object complete (memory heavy, highest fidelity)
  - streaming-merge: merge object fields as they arrive; tolerate overwrites by last-writer-wins and emit synthetic change events
  - schema-driven-commit: using a user-provided JSON Schema (or light spec) commit stable keys earlier and mark others tentative
- For mobile/edge clients, default is schema-driven-commit with small watermarks (commit-on-key-count>=3 or time>=200ms).

SDK ergonomics (JS/TS, mobile notes):
- SDK surface additions: Session.resume({snapshotId, lastSeq}) -> returns an AsyncIterable of frames. Provide helpers: assembleStructured(), subscribeToolEvents(), ackSnapshot(snapshotId).
- Expose a simple opt-in policy object to tune heuristics: {snapshotTtlHint, resumeMode: strict|best-effort, structuredStrategy: streaming|conservative|schema}
- Backpressure and client pacing: SDK should surface a simple backpressure API where app can call frame.pause() / frame.resume() and the socket will signal the server via a small flow-control frame. Server should throttle generation when client signals pause (not queue unlimited work).
- Failure modes: SDK must make it trivial to opt into auto-retry for resume attempts with exponential backoff and jitter and have clear visible state so product teams can instrument UX (e.g., show "reconnecting—partial reply" vs "resuming could lose content").

Operational considerations and GC:
- Snapshot GC: server maintains a sliding window per-session; snapshots older than config.TTL are marked expired. Offer an admin API to extend a snapshot to a dedicated checkpoint (long-term, billed).
- Telemetry retention: raw tool_event streams are kept for 30 days in hot store; aggregated metrics kept for 1 year. Allow customers to configure longer retention for enterprise.
- Security: snapshots must not contain plaintext PII. Snapshots carry opaque refs; actual sensitive blobs remain customer-side or in encrypted store with KMS.

Edge cases, open questions (brainstorm):
- Q: What if a tool-call is mid-flight and the tool itself is non-idempotent? Do we block resume until the tool either completes or we can reconcile?
  - Idea: add a "tool-safety-level" tag and force checkpoint before non-idempotent tool.
- Q: How to guarantee semantic parity if client rewrites earlier utterances before resuming?
  - Idea: server validates a context-hash supplied by client and fails fast if mismatch; provide merge hints for small edits.
- Q: Long-running tools (>30s) and mobile disconnects: prefer delegation to durable job queue, but UX tradeoff.

Experiment matrix (for alpha):
- Experiment A: short TTL (15s) snapshots with best-effort resume on Hosted free tier; measure resume-success and cost reduction.
- Experiment B: dedicated checkpoint (persisted 24h) option in Dedicated customers; measure adoption and billing opt-ins.
- Experiment C: schema-driven structured commits vs conservative buffering; measure token-latency to first-commit and client mem usage for top 10 customers.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Internal feature gate: implement snapshot frames and resume_preamble in dev cluster; SDK hook in JS running behind feature flag. 2) Small alpha with internal Redwood apps and 3 pilot customers. 3) Expand telemetry sampling and mobile client SDK PoC. 4) Beta with top-tier hosted customers, document operational SLAs.

TODOs (owner: Avery) [short list]:
- [ ] Draft JS SDK API surface (async iterator + reassembler) and share in eng-api-review (link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Wire up minimal telemetry schema in team-observability so dashboards can be prototyped.
- [ ] Decide default snapshot TTLs and GC policy with infra cost estimates.
- [ ] Small security review: ensure no snapshot leaks PII or leads to key exfil.

Notes / colloquial reminders:
- Keep snapshots cheap. Prefer pointer-based metadata to any attempt at serializing full KV caches.
- SDK should favor simplicity: apps should rarely need to manage fragment_seq directly. Provide good defaults and opt-ins for advanced tuning.
- Telemetry must play nice with existing traces (we will attach trace_id when present).

References and inspiration:
- See linked artifacts above; also review: incremental-output playbooks in hosted-api folder and tool-call idempotency notes.
- Slack thread: #hosted-api-arch (search "resume snapshot approach")

Open list of follow-ups for next meeting:
- Align with serving-runtime on whether resume can avoid model re-execution in majority cases (ask runtime: what minimal state needed to continue?).
- Cost model work: simulate snapshot/store and telemetry ingestion costs for 10k sessions / hr.

End of scrapbook.
